<p>
This page broadly covers the Weaviate Python client (
<code>v4</code>
 release). For usage information not specific to the Python client, such as code examples, see the relevant pages in the 
<a class="" href="/weaviate/guides">How-to manuals & Guides</a>
.
</p>
<h2 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="installation">
Installation
<a href="#installation" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Installation" title="Direct link to Installation" translate="no">
​
</a>
</h2>
<p>
The Python client library is developed and tested using Python 3.8+. It is available on 
<a href="https://pypi.org/project/weaviate-client/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="">PyPI.org</a>

<div class="collapsibleContent_i85q">
<h4 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="weaviate-version-compatibility">
Weaviate version compatibility
<a href="#weaviate-version-compatibility" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Weaviate version compatibility" title="Direct link to Weaviate version compatibility" translate="no">​</a>
</h4>
<p>
The 
<code>v4</code>
 Python client requires Weaviate 
<code>v1.23.7</code>
 and later. Generally, we encourage you to use the latest version of the Python client and the Weaviate Database.
</p>
<p>
In Weaviate Cloud, clusters are compatible with the 
<code>v4</code>
 client as of 31 January, 2024. Clusters created before this date will not be compatible with the 
<code>v4</code>
 client.
</p>
<h4 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="grpc">
gRPC
<a href="#grpc" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to gRPC" title="Direct link to gRPC" translate="no">​</a>
</h4>
<p>
The 
<code>v4</code>
 client uses remote procedure calls (RPCs) under-the-hood. Accordingly, a port for gRPC must be open to your Weaviate server.
</p>

Prerequisites

<div class="admonitionContent_BuS1">
<p>

<a class="" href="/weaviate/quickstart">
<strong>Quickstart tutorial</strong>
</a>
 first to get the most out of this section.
</p>
</div>
</div>
<p>Get started with Weaviate using this Python example. The code walks you through these key steps:</p>
<ol>
<li class="">
<strong>
<a class="" href="/weaviate/connections">Connect to Weaviate</a>
</strong>
: Establish a connection to a local (or Cloud) Weaviate instance.
</li>
<li class="">
<strong>
<a class="" href="/weaviate/manage-collections">Create a collection</a>
</strong>
: Define the data schema for a 
<code>Question</code>
 collection, using an Ollama model to vectorize the data.
</li>
<li class="">
<strong>
<a class="" href="/weaviate/manage-objects/import">Import data</a>
</strong>
: Fetch sample Jeopardy questions and use Weaviate's batch import for efficient ingestion and automatic vector embedding generation.
</li>
<li class="">
<strong>
<a class="" href="/weaviate/search">Search/query the database</a>
</strong>
: Execute a vector search to find questions semantically similar to the query 
<code>biology</code>
.
</li>
</ol>

<h2 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="asynchronous-usage">
Asynchronous usage
<a href="#asynchronous-usage" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Asynchronous usage" title="Direct link to Asynchronous usage" translate="no">
​
</a>
</h2>
<p>
The Python client library provides a synchronous API by default through the 
<code>WeaviateClient</code>
 class, which is covered on this page. An asynchronous API is also available through the 
<code>WeaviateAsyncClient</code>
 class (from 
<code>weaviate-client</code> <code>v4.7.0</code>
 and up). See the 
<a class="" href="/weaviate/client-libraries/python/async">async client API page</a>
 for further details.
</p>

<div class="theme-admonition theme-admonition-caution admonition_xJq3 alert alert--warning">
<div class="admonitionHeading_Gvgb">
<span class="admonitionIcon_Rf37">
<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16">
<path fill-rule="evenodd" d="M8.893 1.5c-.183-.31-.52-.5-.887-.5s-.703.19-.886.5L.138 13.499a.98.98 0 0 0 0 1.001c.193.31.53.501.886.501h13.964c.367 0 .704-.19.877-.5a1.03 1.03 0 0 0 .01-1.002L8.893 1.5zm.133 11.497H6.987v-2.003h2.039v2.003zm0-3.004H6.987V5.987h2.039v4.006z"></path>

</span>
.Vectors.text2vec_xxx with AutoSchema
</div>
<div class="admonitionContent_BuS1">
<p>
Defining a collection with 
<code>Configure.Vectors.text2vec_xxx()</code>
 with Python client library 
<code>4.16.0</code>
-
<code>4.16.3</code>
 will throw an error if no properties are defined and 
<code>vectorize_collection_name</code>
 is not set to 
<code>True</code>
.
</p>
<p>
This is addressed in 
<code>4.16.4</code>
 of the Weaviate Python client. See this FAQ entry for more details: 
<a class="" href="/weaviate/more-resources/faq#q-invalid-properties-error-when-creating-a-collection-python-client-versions-4160-to-4163">Invalid properties error in Python client versions 4.16.0 to 4.16.3</a>
.
</p>
</div>
</div>
<p>
Starting with the Weaviate Python client 
<code>v4.16.0</code>
, there are multiple changes to the vectorizer configuration API when creating collections:
</p>
<ul>
<li class="">
<code>.vectorizer_config</code>
 has been replaced with 
<code>.vector_config</code>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>Configure.NamedVectors</code>
 has been replaced with 
<code>Configure.Vectors</code>
 and 
<code>Configure.MultiVectors</code>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>Configure.NamedVectors.none</code>
 and 
<code>Configure.Vectorizer.none</code>
 have been replaced with 
<code>Configure.Vectors.self_provided</code>
 and 
<code>Configure.MultiVectors.self_provided</code>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="python-client-v3-deprecation">
Python client 
<code>v3</code>
 deprecation
<a href="#python-client-v3-deprecation" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to python-client-v3-deprecation" title="Direct link to python-client-v3-deprecation" translate="no">
​
</a>
</h4>
<p>
The Weaviate Python client 
<code>v3</code>
 has been deprecated and should no longer be used. If you need documentation for the 
<code>v3</code>
 client, see the 
<a href="https://archive.docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/client-libraries/python/python_v3" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="">documentation archive</a>
. If you are migrating from the Python 
<code>v3</code>
 client to the 
<code>v4</code>
 client, see this 
<a href="https://archive.docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/client-libraries/python/v3_v4_migration" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="">migration guide</a>
.
</p>
<h4 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="beta-releases">
Beta releases
<a href="#beta-releases" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Beta releases" title="Direct link to Beta releases" translate="no">
​
</a>
</h4>
<details class="details_lb9f isBrowser_bmU9 alert alert--info details_b_Ee" data-collapsed="true">
<summary>
Migration guides - beta releases
</summary>
<div style="display: none; overflow: hidden; height: 0px;">
<div class="collapsibleContent_i85q">
<h4 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="changes-in-v44b9">
Changes in 
<code>v4.4b9</code>
<a href="#changes-in-v44b9" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to changes-in-v44b9" title="Direct link to changes-in-v44b9" translate="no">​</a>
</h4>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="weaviateconnect_to_x-methods">
<code>weaviate.connect_to_x</code>
 methods
<a href="#weaviateconnect_to_x-methods" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weaviateconnect_to_x-methods" title="Direct link to weaviateconnect_to_x-methods" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>
The 
<code>timeout</code>
 argument in now a part of the 
<code>additional_config</code>
 argument. It takes the class 
<code>weaviate.config.AdditionalConfig</code>
 as input.
</p>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="queries">
Queries
<a href="#queries" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Queries" title="Direct link to Queries" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>
All optional arguments to methods in the 
<code>query</code>
 namespace now are enforced as keyword arguments.
</p>
<p>There is now runtime logic for parsing query arguments enforcing the correct type.</p>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="batch-processing">
Batch processing
<a href="#batch-processing" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Batch processing" title="Direct link to Batch processing" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>Introduction of three distinct algorithms using different batching styles under-the-hood:</p>
<ul>
<li class="">
<code>client.batch.dynamic()</code>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>client.batch.fixed_size()</code>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>client.batch.rate_limit()</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>
<code>client.batch.dynamic() as batch</code>
 is a drop-in replacement for the previous 
<code>client.batch as batch</code>
, which is now deprecated and will be removed on release.
</p>

<p>
<code>client.batch.rate_limit() as batch</code>
 is a new way to help avoid hitting third-party vectorization API rate limits. By specifying 
<code>request_per_minute</code>
 in the

<code>rate_limit()</code>
 method, you can force the batching algorithm to send objects to Weaviate at the speed your third-party API is capable of processing objects.
</p>
<p>
These methods now return completely localized context managers. This means that 
<code>failed_objects</code>
 and 
<code>failed_references</code>
 of one batch won't be included
in any subsequent calls.
</p>
<p>Finally, if the background thread responsible for sending the batches raises an exception this is now re-raised in the main thread rather than silently erroring.</p>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="filters">
Filters
<a href="#filters" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Filters" title="Direct link to Filters" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>
The argument 
<code>prop</code>
 in 
<code>Filter.by_property</code>
 has been renamed to 
<code>name</code>
</p>
<p>
Ref counting is now achievable using 
<code>Filter.by_ref_count(ref)</code>
 rather than 
<code>Filter([ref])</code>
</p>

Library imports

<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="close-client-connections">

<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="batch-processing-1">
Batch processing
<a href="#batch-processing-1" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Batch processing" title="Direct link to Batch processing" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>
The v4.4b7 client introduces changes to 
<code>client.batch</code>
.
</p>
<ul>
<li class="">
<code>client.batch</code>
 requires a context manager.
</li>
<li class="">
Manual mode is removed, you cannot send batches with 
<code>.create_objects</code>
.
</li>
<li class="">
Batch size and the number of concurrent requests are dynamically assigned. Use 
<code>batch.configure_fixed_size</code>
 to specify values.
</li>
<li class="">
The 
<code>add_reference</code>
 method is updated.
</li>
<li class="">
The 
<code>to_object_collection</code>
 method is removed.
</li>
</ul>
<p>
Updated 
<code>client.batch</code>
 parameters
</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Old value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value in v4.4b7</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">from_object_uuid: UUID</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">from_uuid: UUID</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">from_object_collection: str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">from_collection: str</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">from_property_name: str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">from_property: str</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">to_object_uuid: UUID</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">to: Union[WeaviateReference, List[UUID]]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">to_object_collection: Optional[str] = None</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">tenant: Optional[str] = None</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">tenant: Optional[str] = None</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="filter-syntax">
Filter syntax
<a href="#filter-syntax" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Filter syntax" title="Direct link to Filter syntax" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>Filter syntax is updated in v4.4b7.</p>
<p>
<strong>NOTE</strong>
: The 
<a href="#reference-filters" class="">filter reference syntax</a>
 is simplified in 4.4b8.
</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Old syntax</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">New syntax in v4.4b7</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filter(path=property)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filter.by_property(property)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filter(path=["ref", "target_class", "target_property"])</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filter.by_ref().link_on("ref").by_property("target_property")</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">FilterMetadata.ByXX</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">
Filter.by_id()
<br>
 Filter.by_creation_time() 
<br>
 Filter.by_update_time()
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<a href="#references" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to References" title="Direct link to References" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<p>Multi-target references updated. These are the new functions:</p>
<ul>
<li class="">
<code>ReferenceProperty.MultiTarget</code>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>DataReference.MultiTarget</code>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>QueryReference.MultiTarget</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>
Use 
<code>ReferenceToMulti</code>
 for multi-target references.
</p>
<h4 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="older-client-changes">
Older client changes
<a href="#older-client-changes" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Older client changes" title="Direct link to Older client changes" translate="no">​</a>
</h4>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="references-1">
References
<a href="#references-1" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to References" title="Direct link to References" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<ul>
<li class="">
References are now added through a 
<code>references</code>
 parameter during collection creation, object insertion and queries.
</li>
<li class="">
The 
<code>FromReference</code>
 class is now called 
<code>QueryReference</code>
.
</li>
</ul>

<li class="">
<code>vector_index_type</code>
 parameter has been removed.
</li>

<li class="">
<code>vectorize_class_name</code>
 parameter in the

 constructor method is 
<code>vectorize_collection_name</code>
.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>[collection].data.update()</code>
 / 
<code>.replace()</code>
 *args order changed, aiming to accommodate not providing properties when updating.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>[collection].data.reference_add</code>
 / 
<code>.reference_delete</code>
 / 
<code>.reference_replace</code>
 the 
<code>ref</code>
 keyword was renamed to 
<code>to</code>
.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>collections.create()</code>
 / 
<code>get()</code>
: 
<code>data_model</code>
 kwarg to keyword to provide generics was renamed to 
<code>data_model_properties</code>
 .
</li>
<li class="">
<code>[object].metadata.uuid</code>
 is now 
<code>[object].uuid</code>
.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>[object].metadata.creation_time_unix</code>
 is now 
<code>[object].metadata.creation_time</code>
.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>[object].metadata.last_update_time_unix</code>
 is now 
<code>[object].metadata.last_update</code>
.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>quantitizer</code>
 is renamed to 
<code>quantizer</code>
</li>
<li class="">
To request the vector in the returned data, use the 
<code>include_vector</code>
 parameter.
</li>
</ul>
<h5 class="anchor anchorTargetStickyNavbar_Vzrq" id="data-types">
Data types
<a href="#data-types" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Data types" title="Direct link to Data types" translate="no">​</a>
</h5>
<ul>
<li class="">
Time metadata (for creation and last updated time) now returns a 
<code>datetime</code>
 object, and the parameters are renamed to 
<code>creation_time</code>
 and 
<code>last_update_time</code>
 under 
<code>MetadataQuery</code>
.
<ul>
<li class="">
<code>metadata.creation_time.timestamp() * 1000</code>
 will return the same value as before.
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="">
<code>query.fetch_object_by_id()</code>
 now uses gRPC under the hood (rather than REST), and returns objects in the same format as other queries.
</li>
<li class="">
<code>UUID</code>
 and 
<code>DATE</code>
 properties are returned as typed objects.
</li>
</ul>
